title: Specialized libraries and import boundaries
summary: Choose a specialized library and use its package entry point alongside the core engine.

cells: Chart scales, themes, Cartesian/polar charts and tooltips
Nodes, edges, layouts, automata, tapes and runners
2D/3D rigid bodies, constraints and backend adapters
Microsoft Edge synthesis, narration and subtitles

blocks.text: The package builds these as independent entries; they are not re-exported wholesale by the core bundle. Import a library symbol from its own entry and shared primitives from retiam. Exact references identify whether a module is actually reachable through an entry barrel.

Core playgrounds auto-inject core exports. Library examples in this handbook are package-based application code. The built library bundles import the core package by its bare specifier, so a plain browser URL needs an appropriate import map or a bundler; pointing a playground at a library URL alone is insufficient. Run the library demos in the root application/Studio, where Vite resolves the package aliases.

Start with the [focused library scenes](/examples-libraries-media). The complete [repository example collection](/examples-catalog) adds runnable integration modules, dependency-heavy scenes and asset-bearing fixtures with their source and runtime requirements.
Open one chart scene and one graph scene; each uses only its own library.
